previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Symptoms began four days prior with nausea and poor intake, escalating to severe right upper quadrant pain. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis but normal liver and pancreatic enzymes. CT abdomen showed no acute pathology but indicated constipation and findings consistent with congestive hepatopathy and cardiomegaly. Symptoms improved with supportive care, bowel movement, and symptom management. During admission, gross hematuria was noted, with positive BK virus PCR, prompting urology follow-up. The patient stabilized, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with plans for GI and urology outpatient follow-up, medication adjustments including reduced aspirin dose, and continued monitoring of transplant and diabetic complications.

FINDINGS: 

Bilateral interstitial parenchymal opacities and slight cephalization of the
vessels compared to the prior exams suggests mild edema.  A right pleural
effusion is trace and the fissures are thickened, consistent with volume
overload and/or heart failure.  The heart remains enlarged.  Epicardial pacer
leads are appropriately positioned.  The subcutaneous pacer has been removed
in the interim.  The leadless pacer device appears to be in the right
ventricle.  No pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Appropriate position of epicardial pacer leads and newly placed leadless
pacer device in RV.
2.  Cardiomegaly and mild interstitial edema with trace right pleural effusion
consistent with volume overload and/or heart failure.
